topic: Attempt 3 distance-quality metric review and retrospective evaluation gate

review_contract.inclusion_rule: Include work that directly proposes 1/Ratio@k, critiques Recall for ANN evaluation, evaluates downstream vector-search utility, or controls ANN search using a declared quality target.
excluded: generic ranking metrics without ANN evaluation evidence
metric-learning papers that alter the embedding model
new SAQ mechanisms proposed before metric-sensitivity evidence

sources.title: ANN Search: Recall What Matters
sources.finding: Defines 1/Ratio@k as the inverse mean of position-wise returned-to-exact Euclidean-distance ratios; shows lower cost at fixed distance-quality thresholds, while reporting that algorithm rankings remain largely unchanged.

sources.title: Semantic Recall for Vector Search
sources.review_depth: primary abstract and comparison in the inverse-ratio paper
sources.finding: Proposes Semantic Recall and Tolerant Recall to avoid penalizing semantically irrelevant or distance-equivalent misses; the former requires relevance judgments and the latter a tolerance.

sources.title: DARTH: Declarative Recall Through Early Termination for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
sources.finding: Uses adaptive early termination to meet a declarative Recall target for HNSW and IVF. A future ratio-targeted search controller would collide directly and require a distinct mechanism.

sources.title: Towards Robustness: A Critique of Current Vector Database Assessments
sources.review_depth: primary abstract and comparison in the inverse-ratio paper
sources.finding: Defines Robustness-delta@K as the fraction of queries whose Recall exceeds a chosen floor, addressing hidden query tails but retaining identifier Recall and a threshold parameter.

sources.title: Reveal Hidden Pitfalls and Navigate Next Generation of Vector Similarity Search from Task-Centric Views
sources.review_depth: primary abstract and comparison in the inverse-ratio paper
sources.finding: Evaluates vector search with application-specific labels and metrics across realistic tasks; it can reorder methods but requires inputs beyond a standard ANN benchmark.
